design_rationale:
TASK 0 DOSSIER (rework round 3) — resident_trust_fund_accounts (env_0074), frozen 2026-10-21 10:20:00 EDT.

1. WHY THIS IS A GOOD TEST. Carol Vance (POA) asks one thing: let her mother's resident funds account pay toward the Sept 26 van trip bill, as much as it can properly cover today. The figure is a per-bill authorization amount she signs herself (owner=user). Its rule waits, by one state-form prerequisite sentence, on a payer-covered return for the most recent transfer to an ancillary charge, where part of that transfer paid for days a payer covers. The Oct 8 transfer paid the September oxygen concentrator charge; Part A covers that charge's days from 2026-09-09 (the coverage office booked September Oct 1 and the ancillary office credited the Part A days Oct 15), and no payer-covered return names the transfer. The agent must find this, figure and post the return (agent write), then figure the authorization amount on the higher balance. Difficulty is policy reading plus reconciliation across trust, ancillary, Medicare, bed-hold and private records; each problem has exactly one tool.

2. SCOPE. Task 0 claims trust_ext_covered_service_return (return_improper_transfer_e2970e4f, agent, state_due) and trust_ext_ancillary_authorization_amount (sign_bill_payment_authorization_74e4ddf9, user, on_request). Task 1 claims the spare withdrawal and its three prerequisites (see 1.json); scopes are disjoint and cover all extended policies.

3. DRAW (draw_counts.py --task 0): prerequisite_problems=1, factor_counts=[5, 4]. The authorization amount takes 5 factors, the return 4.

4. PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root = authorization amount (user). Prerequisite = covered-service return (agent). Edge value_input on balance_now, state form: "The amount a new per-bill authorization covers is fixed only after the account's ledger carries a payer-covered return for the most recent transfer to an ancillary charge, where part of that transfer paid for days a payer covers." The sentence selects the most recent transfer to an ancillary charge, the row the return policy selects, and is engaged only where the return policy writes a positive amount. Opening: trust_ledger b97eec63 (Oct 8, naming 1e5a41d1); de7ad2fc (Oct 9, amount_error) is the only return naming it; medicare_coverages b053bc47 active from 2026-09-09. Order: return, then authorization. Skip test in prerequisite_closure. Persona never names the oxygen charge, Medicare or a return; tools check nothing.

5. BASE-INVARIANT CARD. Return (subject trust_reversal): trust_evt_reversals return_once "An entry is returned once per reason." — b97eec63 has only an amount_error return, so a payer_covered_item return is allowed; within the improper charge reversal business days after the Oct 15 ancillary credit made the payer's part known. Authorization (subject trust_bill_transfer): authorized_transfer — the account has no standing authorization covering ancillary charges (standing_authorization none), so the van trip charge needs a per-bill authorization naming it; the transfer posts on the second business day after signing, so no transfer is owed today.

6. BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Return: object = the most recent ancillary transfer b97eec63 and the charge it names, 1e5a41d1 (oxygen concentrator, billed from 2026-09-01, 30 days); its payments 36c7a8ef (trust) and dfc17ed4 (check, same date); its Oct 15 consolidated-billing credit (not counted: the account is in the consolidated billing tier, so that credit records the payer's part); the trust-transfer payment the ancillary ledger applied on the transfer's date; no price-error, not-requested or dispute credit; the August charge edae3fb5 and the salon charge f6197e8a are not named by the transfer. Authorization: object = the most recent one-time item charge 4d106878 (van trip, open); the older item f6197e8a excluded.

7. FACTOR CARD - return [expected 67.11; all-baseline 120.00]. payer_start_days (method): an active Part A episode from 2026-09-09; the charge billed from 2026-09-01 for 30 days -> 22 charged days on or after the coverage start -> tier 'a Medicare Part A episode is active'; baseline gives 100.00. credits_counted (parameter): the ancillary account is in the consolidated billing tier; the only credit naming the charge is the Oct 15 consolidated-billing credit of 135.67, so no credit is counted -> tier 'the ancillary account is in the consolidated billing tier'; baseline gives 90.44. transfer_paid_part (parameter): the ancillary ledger carries the Oct 8 payment by trust transfer of 100.00 naming the charge, not more than the 120.00 transfer less the 20.00 returned Oct 9 as a wrong amount (the Oct 6 authorization also states 100.00) -> paid part 100.00 -> tier 'the ancillary ledger carries a payment by trust transfer naming the charge on the transfer's date'; baseline gives 71.06. refund_order (method): the other payment (50.00 check) carries the transfer's own date Oct 8 -> tier 'another payment named the charge on the transfer's own date'; baseline gives 100.00. plain: improper part 185.00 x 22 / 30 = 135.67 (unrounded); unpaid balance 185.00 - 150.00 - 0.00 = 35.00; refundable 100.67; portion 100.67 x 100.00 / 150.00 = 67.11, below the paid part 100.00.

8. FACTOR CARD - authorization amount [expected 56.11; all-baseline 0.00]. covered_run_end (method): no last covered date; a bed hold in progress since 2026-10-19 -> the run (from 10-01, the day after the September block) ends 10-18 = 18 days -> tier 'no such date is set and a bed hold is in progress because the resident is away'; baseline gives 0.00. coinsurance_share (parameter): Medigap Plan K, no QMB -> 50 -> tier 'Medigap Plan K with no QMB status'; baseline gives 0.00. run_start_day (method): the coverage office booked September (09-09..09-30) on Oct 1, the episode's most recent booked block ending 09-30 -> the run starts 10-01 -> tier 'a block of the active episode is booked'; baseline gives 0.00. hold_first_night (method): the hold's first held day is 2026-10-19 (private hold start); the transfer notice was delivered 2026-10-20 09:00, after it -> the first night allowed is 10-20, so 1 night (10-20) builds up -> tier 'the latest transfer notice recorded for the reservation was delivered after the hold's first held day'; baseline gives 0.00. held_room_tier (parameter): the reservation records Semi-Private Long-Term Care Room held (398.00 on the 2026-07-01 schedule); the agreement is a private room -> tier 'the reservation in progress records the room tier held'; baseline gives 18.11. plain: Plan K took effect 2026-10-06, after the run's first day, so 10-01..10-05 (5 days) keep the whole coinsurance and 10-06..10-18 (13 days) take the share; run 10-01..10-18 at the 2026 rate 217.00; numbering 18 prior SNF days + 22 booked days before the run -> the run's days are benefit days 41-58, all coinsurance days; run-up 217.00 x (5 x 100 + 13 x 50) / 100 = 2495.50; held 1 x 398.00 = 398.00; balance after the return 2949.61; spare 2949.61 - 2495.50 - 398.00 = 56.11; the van trip charge's open balance 115.70 -> 56.11.

9. WHY EACH CLASS OF SEED ROW EXISTS. Trust: balance from two family checks, two interest credits recomputed from daily balances, petty-cash and check withdrawals (the Oct 16 check withdrawal included), the Oct 8 transfer and the Oct 9 wrong-amount return. Medicare: the earlier episode Jul 28 - Aug 14 (18 days in band 1-20) gives the prior SNF days; the active episode from 09-09 with September booked Oct 1 and its coinsurance (20 days at the 2026 rate) paid, Plan K from 10-06. Ancillary: Part B tier while private, consolidated billing tier from 09-09 with the Oct 15 credit of the September Part A days, concentrator August/September charges, salon and van trip. Bed-hold: the Medicare skilled-stay hospital hold in progress, its transfer notice delivered the morning after the departure. Private: private room from Aug 15, conversion credit from Sept 9, deposit and credit balance refunded. Every correction another office owes before the opening is posted; the trust's own return is the only owed write.

10. PERSONA. Carol speaks for herself as POA, brisk and friendly; volunteers only the van trip bill and the wish that the account pay as much as it properly can; identity details on request; passive agreement if told money must be put back first; signs the authorization herself for the amount given; ends on the recorded authorization.

11. STANDARD SOLUTION. Locate and verify; read the trust account, ledger and requests; the ancillary account, ledger and requests; the Medicare coverages and both episodes' ledgers; the bed-hold reservations, ledger and elections; the private agreement and ledger. Post the payer-covered return naming b97eec63; hand over the authorization; Carol signs the authorization amount for the van trip charge.

12. EASY MISTAKES. Returning the whole transfer or its paid part; counting every charged day as covered; counting the consolidated-billing credit against the unpaid balance; taking the whole 120.00 transfer instead of the 100.00 the ancillary ledger applied; giving the transfer the whole refundable part although the check came the same day; numbering the run from day 1 or ignoring the September block; putting every October coinsurance day at the Plan K share although Plan K took effect 10-06; ending the run yesterday instead of before the leave; starting the run on the coverage start date instead of after the booked September block; counting the Oct 19 night held before the notice was delivered; pricing the held nights at the agreement's private room; signing the van trip's whole open balance.

13. VERIFICATION. check_compute recomputes both computations on the handling-time world (gold writes replayed with the real tools); the scratch replay matched the expected values and the per-factor baselines above.

14. CLOSURE. Return -> return_improper_transfer_e2970e4f -> amount -> trust_reversal payer_covered_item naming b97eec63; authorization -> sign_bill_payment_authorization_74e4ddf9 -> amount -> bill_payment_authorization naming 4d106878. required_documents = charter_scope.extended_policies = computation policy ids.

15. REVISION (round 2). Factors and world rebuilt after audit revision_1; superseded in round 3 (section 16).


16. REVISION (round 3). Audit revision_2: the prerequisite sentence selects the return policy's own row and is engaged only where the return is positive (R2-1); September booked and the other offices' Part A corrections posted, so nothing another office owes is pending (T0-R2-X1, T0-X1); the run is numbered as the coverage office numbers it, priced per day of service, and a completed leave inside the run stops the run-up (R2-2, R2-3, R2-7); P2 factors rebuilt (Plan K effective date split, held room tier, uncharged held nights); the return's nights-away factor removed (R2-4) and credits-counted added; rounding RND(x + 0.000000001, 2), tools use an exact Decimal half-up helper.

17. REVISION (round 6). Audit revision_5 (R3-2, R5-1): the return's paid part is read from the ancillary ledger's applied trust-transfer payment, else the authorization's amount, else the whole transfer; the credits counted follow the ancillary account's tier (the credit of the tier's own payer is the improper part; another payer's coverage credit settles the charge); the authorization amount's share split and held-night factors became plain sentences and two factors replace them: the daily coinsurance rate by year of service (superseded in round 9: now a plain sentence) and the first held night the transfer notice allows (notice delivered Oct 20 09:00, after the Oct 19 departure). The Oct 16 check withdrawal is 2035.00 so the spare balance stays below the van trip's open balance.

18. REVISION (round 9). KB audit S3: the September coinsurance charge is seeded as the Medicare rules produce it (20 x 217.00 = 4340.00), so the year-rate rule no longer bears weight on this world and is a plain sentence; the run's first day (after the most recent booked block, else the coverage start) is the factor in its place. S6: the held semi-private bed versus the converted private-room agreement rests on private_tier_placement 'Only an open, active agreement changes tier' (seed-consistency entry). Figures unchanged.
user_scenario: You are Carol Vance, the daughter of Margaret Szymanski, who lives at the Keystone Ridge center in Lancaster. You hold your mother's power of attorney and you look after her money, and you are calling the business office on a weekday morning between work meetings, brisk but friendly. A bill came for the van trip your mother took on Saturday, September 26, and you want her resident funds account at the center to pay toward that van trip bill, as much as her account can properly cover today. You leave the figure to the office; you have no idea what it should be and you do not suggest one. If the agent asks who is calling, you say you are her daughter and her agent under a power of attorney. To find and confirm her record you give her full name, Margaret Szymanski, and her date of birth, 1941-05-23; if a second detail is wanted you give the last four of her Social Security number, 5276, and only if yet another detail is asked for do you give the billing phone on file, 717-555-0531. If the agent explains that some money taken from her account has to be put back into it first, you say that is fine with you and let them go ahead. When the agent tells you how much the account can put toward the van trip and hands you the authorization to sign, you sign it yourself as her power of attorney for exactly the amount the agent gives you; if that is less than the whole bill you simply say you understand. Once the agent tells you the authorization is recorded, you thank them and end the call.

edges.condition: The trust ledger carries a trust_reversal with reason payer_covered_item naming the most recent trust_bill_transfer to an ancillary charge, where the transfer's portion of the part of that charge a payer covers is above zero.
edges.policy_source: The amount a new per-bill authorization covers is fixed only after the account's ledger carries a payer-covered return for the most recent transfer to an ancillary charge, where part of that transfer paid for days a payer covers.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The Oct 8 transfer is the most recent transfer to an ancillary charge and paid the September oxygen concentrator charge billed from 2026-09-01; the Part A episode covers that charge's days from 2026-09-09 (the coverage office booked them Oct 1 and the ancillary office credited them Oct 15), so part of the transfer paid for days a payer covers; the only return naming the transfer is the Oct 9 amount_error return - no payer-covered return exists.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The return tool records a payer_covered_item return naming the Oct 8 transfer, which raises the account balance by the amount returned.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: Single edge, no parallel prerequisites: the prerequisite sentence fixes the authorization amount only after the return stands, and the authorization amount is evaluated on the world after the return.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Without the return the spare balance falls below zero and the authorization amount moves from 56.11 to 0.00.
